previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with multiple comorbidities, including severe COPD, diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, obesity hypoventilation syndrome, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted due to altered mental status and hypoxia. She was found agitated and noncompliant with oxygen at her nursing home, leading to respiratory acidosis and acute kidney injury. She required intubation for hypercapnic respiratory failure but was extubated the next day. Encephalopathy was attributed to hypercarbia and accumulation of opioid metabolites due to reduced kidney function. Her kidney injury resolved with IV fluids and medication adjustments. A urinary tract infection was suspected initially, but cultures grew only yeast, so antibiotics were discontinued. She was stabilized on home oxygen, her pain regimen was simplified to avoid sedating opioids, and she was discharged to extended care with improved mental status and renal function.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Ulcer of other part of lower limb
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms ___,

It was a pleasure to care for you at ___. You were admitted to 
the hospital because you were having difficulty breathing. You 
were found to have the flu (influenza) and some volume overload 
from your heart failure. You were treated with lasix (a 'water 
pill') for the extra fluid in your lungs,  and nebulizer 
treatments to also help your breathing. We continued your other 
home medications. When your breathing improved you were 
transferred from the ICU to the regular medicine floor. You were 
treated with 5 days of prednisone for a COPD exacerbation from 
your flu, and given regular nebulizing treatments, and your 
symptoms improved. You unfortunately were not able to tolerate 
CPAP. 

You should continue taking your medications and follow up with 
your physicians.

We wish you all the best.

-Your ___ care team
